title_th: การซื้อเสื้อผ้า
recycles: polite requests with Can I / Could I
Sorry, could you say that again?
present continuous for what you're doing now
register: Friendly service register — polite but relaxed; first-name-free, no honorifics, short direct requests

targets.why_it_matters_here: Thai finals are unreleased, so 'Do you have a large size?' comes out as 'lar' 'sigh' and the assistant brings the wrong garment or nothing at all. At the till, 'card' said as 'car' makes staff ask twice or hand you a cash total, and 'receipt' without the final /t/ loses you the proof you need to exchange a sale item.

Thai speakers flatten English diphthongs, so 'It's on sale' sounds like 'It's on sell' and 'thirty-eight' sounds like 'thirty-eat' — you pay the wrong price or agree to the wrong item. Asking for a 'coat' but saying 'cot', or 'white' but saying 'wet', sends the assistant to the wrong shelf while you wait.

เสื้อโค้ท / เสื้อแจ็คเก็ต ใส่คลุมกันหนาว

model_dialogues.label: Buying a shirt — the standard sequence

lines.speaker: Assistant
lines.text: Hi! Can I help you find anything?
lines.th: สวัสดีค่ะ กำลังหาอะไรอยู่รึเปล่าคะ

lines.speaker: Learner
lines.text: Yes, I like this shirt. Do you have a large?
lines.th: ค่ะ ชอบเสื้อตัวนี้ มีไซซ์ L ไหม

lines.speaker: Assistant
lines.text: Let me check. Yep, here's a large in black.
lines.th: ขอเช็คแป๊บนะคะ มีค่ะ นี่ไซซ์ L สีดำ

lines.speaker: Learner
lines.text: Thanks. Can I try it on?
lines.th: ขอบคุณค่ะ ขอลองได้ไหม

lines.speaker: Assistant
lines.text: Sure, the fitting room is on the right.
lines.th: ได้เลยค่ะ ห้องลองอยู่ทางขวา

lines.speaker: Learner
lines.text: It's a bit tight. Do you have a bigger size?
lines.th: คับไปนิดนึง มีใหญ่กว่านี้ไหม

lines.speaker: Assistant
lines.text: I've got an extra large, but only in grey.
lines.th: มี XL ค่ะ แต่เหลือแค่สีเทา

lines.speaker: Learner
lines.text: That's fine. I'll take the grey one. How much is it?
lines.th: ไม่เป็นไร เอาสีเทาก็ได้ ราคาเท่าไหร่

lines.speaker: Assistant
lines.text: It's on sale — twenty-eight ninety-five.
lines.th: กำลังลดราคาอยู่ค่ะ 28.95

lines.speaker: Learner
lines.text: Great. Can I pay by card?
lines.th: ดีเลย จ่ายบัตรได้ไหม

model_dialogues.label: Buying a coat — the size is out of stock and it's a final-sale item

lines.speaker: Assistant
lines.text: Hi there, are you after anything in particular?
lines.th: สวัสดีค่ะ มองหาอะไรอยู่รึเปล่าคะ

lines.speaker: Learner
lines.text: Yes, I'm looking for a coat. Something warm.
lines.th: ค่ะ หาเสื้อโค้ทอยู่ เอาแบบอุ่นๆ

lines.speaker: Assistant
lines.text: These ones just came in. What size are you?
lines.th: ตัวพวกนี้เพิ่งเข้าใหม่เลยค่ะ ใส่ไซซ์อะไรคะ

lines.speaker: Learner
lines.text: Medium, I think. Can I try this white one?
lines.th: น่าจะ M มั้ง ขอลองตัวสีขาวนี้ได้ไหม

lines.speaker: Assistant
lines.text: Of course. The fitting rooms are just past the shoes.
lines.th: ได้เลยค่ะ ห้องลองอยู่เลยตรงรองเท้าไปนิดเดียว

lines.speaker: Learner
lines.text: The sleeves are too long. Do you have a small?
lines.th: แขนยาวไป มีไซซ์ S ไหม

lines.speaker: Assistant
lines.text: Sorry, we're out of small in white. I've got small in grey and navy.
lines.th: ขอโทษค่ะ สีขาวไซซ์ S หมด เหลือ S สีเทากับสีกรมท่า

lines.speaker: Learner
lines.text: Hmm. Can you check another shop?
lines.th: อืม... ช่วยเช็คสาขาอื่นให้หน่อยได้ไหม

lines.speaker: Assistant
lines.text: I can order the white one online — it'd get here Thursday.
lines.th: สั่งออนไลน์ตัวสีขาวให้ได้นะคะ น่าจะถึงวันพฤหัสฯ

lines.speaker: Learner
lines.text: How much is delivery?
lines.th: ค่าส่งเท่าไหร่

lines.speaker: Assistant
lines.text: Free over fifty. But online it's not on sale, I'm afraid.
lines.th: เกิน 50 ส่งฟรีค่ะ แต่ซื้อออนไลน์จะไม่ได้ราคาลดนะคะ

lines.speaker: Learner
lines.text: So the grey one is cheaper today?
lines.th: งั้นวันนี้สีเทาถูกกว่าใช่ไหม

lines.speaker: Assistant
lines.text: Yeah — grey's thirty-eight, the white one's forty-five online.
lines.th: ใช่ค่ะ สีเทา 38 ส่วนสีขาวออนไลน์ 45

lines.speaker: Learner
lines.text: Sorry, thirty-eight or forty-eight?
lines.th: โทษที 38 หรือ 48 นะ

lines.speaker: Assistant
lines.text: Thirty-eight. Three, eight.
lines.th: 38 ค่ะ สาม-แปด

lines.speaker: Learner
lines.text: Okay. I'll take the grey small.
lines.th: โอเค เอาสีเทาไซซ์ S

lines.speaker: Assistant
lines.text: Nice choice. Just so you know, sale items are exchange only.
lines.th: เลือกได้ดีค่ะ บอกไว้ก่อนนะคะ ของลดราคาเปลี่ยนได้อย่างเดียว คืนเงินไม่ได้

lines.speaker: Learner
lines.text: Can I exchange it if it doesn't fit?
lines.th: ถ้าใส่ไม่พอดี เอามาเปลี่ยนได้ใช่ไหม

lines.speaker: Assistant
lines.text: Yep, within fourteen days, and you'll need the receipt.
lines.th: ได้ค่ะ ภายใน 14 วัน แล้วต้องเอาใบเสร็จมาด้วยนะคะ

lines.speaker: Learner
lines.text: That's fine. Can I pay by card?
lines.th: โอเคค่ะ จ่ายบัตรได้ไหม

chunk_drills.label: Asking for a size or colour
examples: Do you have this in a large?
Do you have this in black?
Do you have this in a smaller size?
Do you have these in an eight?
chunk_drills.spiralled_grammar: Yes/No questions with 'do' + this/these (recycled from shop and café units); singular vs plural item words (shirt / jeans)

chunk_drills.label: Asking to try something on
examples: Can I try these shoes on?
chunk_drills.spiralled_grammar: Polite requests with Can I / Could I (recycled from asking_for_help_politely); object pronoun between verb and 'on'

chunk_drills.label: Saying what's wrong with the fit
chunk_drills.spiralled_grammar: too + adjective vs a bit + adjective for softening; present simple 'it fits'

chunk_drills.label: Checking the price and the number
chunk_drills.pattern: How much is ___? / Sorry, is that ___ or ___?
examples: Sorry, is that thirty or thirteen?
Sorry, is that fifteen or fifty?
chunk_drills.spiralled_grammar: How much is/are + singular/plural (recycled from numbers_and_prices); alternative questions with 'or' for repair

chunk_drills.label: Buying, returning, exchanging
chunk_drills.pattern: I'll take ___. / Can I return it if ___?
examples: Can I return it if it doesn't fit?
Can I exchange it if the size is wrong?
Could I have a receipt, please?
chunk_drills.spiralled_grammar: 'I'll' for decisions made now; first conditional 'if it doesn't fit' with present simple in the if-clause

guided_roleplay.learner_role: A customer buying one item of clothing in a mid-size high-street shop, with on-screen frames and a hint button
flow: Step 1 — Greet the assistant and say what you want (or say 'I'm just looking, thanks').
Step 2 — Ask for your size and colour.
Step 3 — Ask to try it on and find the fitting room.
Step 4 — Come out and describe the fit problem; ask for a different size or colour.
Step 5 — Handle the complication (out of stock / different price / sale item) and check the number you heard.
Step 6 — Say you'll take it, ask about paying, and ask the return or exchange rule.
sentence_frames: It's too ___. Do you have a bigger size?
Can I return it if it doesn't fit?

free_roleplay.ai_persona: A friendly, slightly busy shop assistant in a high-street clothing store. Warm, uses short casual service language ('No worries', 'Let me check for you'), speaks at natural speed, and does not slow down unless the learner asks.
free_roleplay.a2_behavior: Stays on the standard sequence: greets, finds the size, points to the fitting room, confirms the fit, states a clear price, takes payment.
b1_curveballs: The size the learner wants is out of stock; only another colour is available.
Says a price fast with a confusable number ('thirty-eight' / 'forty-eight') and waits to see if the learner checks.
Explains that sale items are exchange only and a receipt is needed.
Offers to order the item online and asks for a delivery address and phone number.
Asks 'Would you like to try the next size up?' and then asks how it feels in detail (shoulders, sleeves, waist).
The card payment fails and the learner must offer cash or another card.
Offers a loyalty card sign-up the learner has to politely decline.

roleplay_rubric.criterion: Completed all six sub-steps: stated the need, asked for a size, asked to try it on, described the fit, handled the complication, paid
Asked for a specific size and colour (not just pointing or saying 'this one')
Described the fit problem with too/a bit + adjective and asked for an alternative
Confirmed the price or number with a repair question ('Sorry, is that thirty or thirteen?') at least once
Asked at least one transaction question: payment method, receipt, or return/exchange rule
Register stayed polite-casual: used 'Can I / Could I / please / thanks', no bare commands
Pronunciation: final consonants on size, large, coat, card, receipt released; diphthongs in sale, eight, white, grey, try clearly distinct
Coped with an off-script curveball (out of stock, failed payment, exchange-only rule) and kept the conversation going to a decision

register_culture_note.en: In most fixed-price shops, staff greet you first and expect a short, friendly answer — 'I'm just looking, thanks' is completely normal and not rude. You do not need formal language; 'Can I try this on?' with 'please' or 'thanks' is exactly right. Trying clothes on, asking for another size, and walking out without buying are all expected behaviour, not an imposition. Prices are fixed in chain stores, so asking for a discount is unusual — ask 'Is this on sale?' instead. Do ask about returns and receipts before you pay; staff answer this question all day long.

do_dont.prefer: Do you have this in a large, please?

do_dont.avoid: Nodding and saying yes when you didn't catch the price
do_dont.prefer: Sorry, is that thirty or thirteen?

do_dont.avoid: Saying 'sigh' or 'lar' with no final sound
do_dont.prefer: Say the final sound: si-ZE, lar-JE, coa-T, car-D

do_dont.avoid: Buying something that doesn't fit because you feel embarrassed

register_culture_note.thai_cultural_note: In Thai markets, bargaining is normal and trying clothes on is often not possible, so many Thai learners either haggle in a fixed-price shop or skip the fitting room and buy the wrong size. In most global chain stores the opposite is true: the price will not move, but trying on, changing your mind and returning an item are all built into the system. Also, accepting help from an assistant does not oblige you to buy — leaving with a simple 'Thanks, I'll think about it' is polite and expected, not a loss of face for either side.

can_do_checkpoints.statement: I can say what item I'm looking for and ask for a specific size and colour.
I can ask to try something on and find the fitting room.
I can ask how much something is and understand a spoken price.
I can describe a fit problem in detail and ask for a different size, colour or item.
I can handle a complication — out of stock, a sale price, exchange-only — and still reach a decision.
I can ask about payment, receipts and the return or exchange policy before I buy.
My final consonants (size, large, coat, card, receipt) and my diphthongs (sale, eight, white, grey) are clear enough that the assistant brings the right item at the right price.
